text: They came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out of the tombs to meet him.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could restrain him any longer, not even with a chain.
He had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he tore the chains apart and smashed the shackles to pieces. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
Night and day, without ceasing, he was among the tombs and in the hills, screaming and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell down before him,
crying out at the top of his voice, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you by God, do not torment me!"
For Jesus had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!"
Then he asked him, "What is your name?" He answered, "My name is Legion, for we are many."
And he begged him urgently not to send them out of the region.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside,
and the spirits begged him, "Send us into the pigs. Let us enter them."
He gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd—about two thousand of them—rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned there.
The herdsmen fled and spread the news in the town and in the countryside, and the people came out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by the legion sitting there, dressed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs as well.
Then they began to beg Jesus to leave their district.
As he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed begged to stay with him.

versions.text: As he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed begged to go with him.
versions.explanation: The Greek says he begged 'that he might be with him' — the emphasis is on remaining in Jesus' company, not merely traveling in the boat. 'Stay with him' captures this and also makes the contrast with Jesus' command in v.19 ('Go home') clearer for oral reading.

text: But Jesus would not allow it. "Go home to your own people," he said, "and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you."
So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
When Jesus had crossed back in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him while he was by the sea.
One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw Jesus he fell at his feet
and pleaded with him urgently: "My little daughter is dying. Please come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be healed and live."
So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed in around him.
Among them was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had endured much under many physicians and had spent all she had, yet instead of getting better she had only grown worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak,
for she said to herself, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Immediately the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was cured of her affliction.
At once Jesus, aware within himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"

versions.text: At once Jesus, aware that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"
versions.explanation: The phrase ἐν ἑαυτῷ ('in himself') is not represented in the translation; it underlines that Jesus perceived this inwardly, an important detail in Mark's account.

text: His disciples said to him, "You see the crowd pressing in on you, and you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But he kept looking around to see who had done it.
Then the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be free from your affliction."

versions.text: He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be free from your affliction."
versions.explanation: The same verb (σῴζω) is rendered 'healed' in verses 23 and 28 but 'saved' here, which is inconsistent within the chapter. In this healing context 'made you well' matches the immediate sense of the narrative; a footnote could note that the verb also means 'saved.'

text: While he was still speaking, messengers came from the house of the synagogue leader and said, "Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the teacher any further?"
But Jesus, overhearing what was said, told the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid; only believe."
He let no one go with him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
They came to the house of the synagogue leader, and Jesus saw the commotion—people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went in and said to them, "Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead but asleep."
They laughed at him. But he put them all outside and took the child's father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child was.
Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, "Talitha koum!"—which means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!"

versions.text: Taking her by the hand, he said to her, "Talitha koum!"—which means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up!"
versions.explanation: The Greek specifies 'the hand of the child' (τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου); naming the child again aids clarity in oral reading after the list of people in v.40. A footnote explaining that 'Talitha koum' is Aramaic would also help hearers.

text: Immediately the girl stood up and began to walk, for she was twelve years old. And they were utterly astonished.
He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this, and he told them to give her something to eat.
